clue.text: Plant book by famous author

indicators.note: by means next to, so the book sits beside the author, here following him

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, the English novelist who wrote Tess of the d'Urbervilles
an annual is a book published once a year, such as a children's Christmas album

explanation.surface: A gardening volume written by a celebrated novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant book' reads as one phrase, but only 'Plant' defines; 'by' places the yearly book alongside the novelist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: gardeners use this term for a species that survives frost and lives for one season.

clue.text: Help given by sailor to little monster

indicators.note: to means one piece is attached to the other, sailor first

parts.note: AB is the abbreviation for able-bodied seaman
ET is the small alien creature of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: A seaman lends a hand to a naughty child.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given by' links definition to wordplay; 'to' joins the seaman's abbreviation to the film alien, who is little and, loosely, a monster.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to assist or encourage someone, usually in wrongdoing.

clue.text: Obligation of little lady met finally

parts.note: Deb is the short form of the woman's name Deborah, and also of debutante

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of the word beside it

explanation.surface: A small woman at last fulfils a duty she owed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' signals a shortened woman's name; 'finally' takes the closing letter of 'met'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something owed, whether money or a moral duty.

clue.text: Hermit with strange cat is hanging around church

indicators.note: hanging around means these letters loiter on the outside of the church
strange means the letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
CE is the abbreviation for Church of England

explanation.surface: A recluse and his odd pet loiter near the chapel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' makes ASTIC, which 'hanging around' sets outside the Church of England's initials; 'with' is only a link. The surface suggests loitering, not enclosing.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a recluse commonly lives in severe self-denial, which is what this noun names.

clue.text: No American can demonstrate common sense

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States, used as an adjective

explanation.surface: Nobody from the States is able to show any practical wisdom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can demonstrate' simply links the two pieces to the definition; the surface insult is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: British slang, from Greek, for practical intelligence or gumption.

clue.text: Goddess like loose woman with little energy

parts.note: like and as are interchangeable in comparisons
tart is British slang for a promiscuous woman
E is the physics abbreviation for energy, little marking the shortening

explanation.surface: A deity resembling a promiscuous girl who tires easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' just joins the pieces; 'little' marks energy as abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: she was the Phoenician deity of fertility and love.

clue.text: Writer spilt ale, messy pup!

indicators.note: something spilt is scattered about, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An author knocks over his beer and scolds the untidy young dog.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation dresses the clue as a scolding. 'spilt' is the signal, coming before the three words it disturbs, though the adjective after it looks more like one.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the seventeenth-century London diarist who recorded the Great Fire.

clue.text: Against team circle, all in all

parts.note: con is the opposing side in pros and cons
a side is a sports team in British usage
a ring is a circular shape

explanation.surface: Opposing a squad standing in a ring, on the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: tacked on to a sentence, both mean taking everything into account.

clue.text: Woman with nothing on — should be dressing!

indicators.note: with says the woman's name is accompanied by the next piece, which follows it

parts.note: May is a woman's given name
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A lady is wearing no clothes and ought to be putting some on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the name to the zero; 'on — should be' merely leads to the definition. 'dressing' is a sauce, not getting clothed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the short name of the egg-and-oil sauce spooned over salads.

clue.text: Football team cut nerdy boy off

indicators.note: off means not right or spoiled, so the preceding letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soccer club drops a geeky lad from the squad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' at the end rearranges CUT NERDY BOY. The club plays in the English Midlands and is nicknamed the Rams.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an English professional soccer club founded in 1884.

clue.text: Endlessly damn despicable people

indicators.note: endlessly means the word for damn loses its final letter

parts.note: to damn someone is to curse them

explanation.surface: Forever condemning contemptible folk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' looks like 'forever' but removes the final E of CURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: literally mongrel dogs, used figuratively for contemptible men.

clue.text: Professional job in theory

parts.note: pro is the short form of professional
a position is a post of employment

explanation.surface: Expert work, at least on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in theory' reads as 'on paper', but 'in' is a link and 'theory' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a statement put forward for consideration, like a hypothesis.

clue.text: Learning 'phi' and 'rho', class may get get confused

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the three words before it have their letters mixed (the clue prints get twice)

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Students studying Greek letters are liable to mix them up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may get get confused' rearranges PHI, RHO and CLASS; 'and' only joins the fodder words.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: academic study or erudition.

clue.text: Recover about 150 before the end

indicators.note: before fixes the order: the first two pieces precede the last one

parts.note: re means concerning, about
CL is 150 in Roman numerals
an end is a goal or aim, as in the means to an end

explanation.surface: Get back roughly 150 just ahead of the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' only fixes the order of the pieces. The surface suggests a finish line, but an end here is a purpose, as in 'to what end?'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to get back something lost or taken.

clue.text: Scot takes a wife, a brightly coloured bird

parts.note: Mac is a conventional name for a Scotsman, from the surname prefix
W is the genealogical abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: A Scotsman marries, and his bride is rather gaudy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' just adds the next pieces to the Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a large long-tailed tropical American parrot with vivid plumage.

clue.text: Like many a horse making attempt, went out in front

parts.note: to have a stab at something is to try it
the runner who led was ahead of the field

explanation.surface: A typical racer makes its effort and takes the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' links the definition to the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: most such animals are kept in stalls in a yard.

clue.text: Criticise son not on time

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
someone not on time is late

explanation.surface: Tell off a boy for being unpunctual.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: British informal verb meaning to attack harshly in a review.

clue.text: Old-fashioned message from a prominent libdem

definitions.meaning: a telegram sent by undersea wire, a form of communication now obsolete
Vince, a leading figure and later leader of Britain's Liberal Democrat party

explanation.definitionFit: Both a telegram sent overseas and the surname of Vince, the British Liberal Democrat politician.

clue.text: Secret scheme to get a piece of ground

definitions.meaning: a small marked-out area of land, as for building or growing vegetables

explanation.definitionFit: Both a conspiracy and a small patch of land carry this name.

clue.text: Drink in Devon's coastal village

definitions.meaning: ale or lager, brewed from malt and hops
a fishing village on the south coast of Devon, an English county

explanation.definitionFit: Both the brewed alcoholic beverage and a real seaside place in south-west England.

clue.text: Note about Italian religion

indicators.note: about means the note is placed round the Italian piece

parts.note: fah is the fourth note of the sol-fa scale
IT is the abbreviation for Italian, as with vermouth in gin and It

explanation.surface: A memo concerning the beliefs held in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning' but is the container signal, and the opening word is a musical one from the sol-fa scale, not a memo.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a system of belief, as in the Christian or Muslim one.

clue.text: Silly swimmer holding gents up?

indicators.note: holding means the swimmer contains the other piece

parts.note: a fish is a creature that swims

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word for gents is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the gents is British for a men's public toilet, a loo

explanation.surface: A daft bather detaining men in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' gives OOL from the British word for a toilet, and 'holding' sets it within the sea creature. The question mark excuses the cheeky picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: lacking good sense.

clue.text: What farmer uses for binding? It's not working properly

definitions.meaning: the strand of metal used to tie up bales of dried grass
out of control or malfunctioning, as a machine may go

explanation.definitionFit: Literally metal strand for tying bales, and as an adjective erratic or out of order.

clue.text: Bird and pig fed salmon!

indicators.note: fed means the pig has been given the fish to swallow, so it goes inside

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A fowl and a hog are both given expensive fish for dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fed' is the container signal: the animal has swallowed the fish, a juvenile one. 'and' joins definition to wordplay, though the surface lists two diners.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a small brown member of the finch-like family common in towns.

clue.text: Peer comes to that just after the start?

parts.note: an earl is a rank of the British nobility
yon is an old or dialect word for that, as in yon hill

explanation.surface: A lord arrives at that point shortly after things begin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes to' joins the nobleman to the dialect word for 'that'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym phrase: at an initial stage of proceedings.

clue.text: Shy d-drunk rolling around

indicators.note: rolling around means the stammered word is turned right over, back to front

parts.note: a drunk is a sot, and the stammer doubles its opening letter as the clue does

explanation.surface: A bashful, stammering tippler staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rolling around' turns S-SOT, the stammered drunkard, backwards. 'Shy' is the verb to throw, as at a coconut shy.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym as a verb: to throw or fling something.

clue.text: Leeds to Portsmouth? There must be a break somewhere

indicators.note: somewhere says the answer is to be found at some point along the journey's words

explanation.surface: A long English drive from north to south needs a rest on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somewhere' points into 'Leeds to Portsmouth', where the answer runs across the three words. Leeds is in northern England and Portsmouth on the south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a halt or pause in a journey.

clue.text: President in the wilderness?

definitions.meaning: either George, father or son, who held the White House
wild uncultivated country, as in the Australian outback

explanation.definitionFit: Both the surname of two American leaders and the word for wild uncleared country.

clue.text: A medic turns up for last bit of work

indicators.note: in a down entry, turns up means both pieces together are read from the bottom

parts.note: doc is short for doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor arrives to finish off the final part of the job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reads A DOC backwards as a whole. The 'work' is a musical composition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the concluding passage of a piece of music.

clue.text: Car part coming from supplier to retailer

definitions.meaning: the device that sends current to each spark plug in turn
a wholesaler who passes goods on to shops

explanation.definitionFit: Both the engine component routing current to spark plugs and a wholesaler.

clue.text: Old piece, brief account of someone's life

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old, as in OT for Old Testament
a bit is a small piece

explanation.surface: An ancient article giving a short biography.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the short form of obituary, a death notice summarising a career.

clue.text: Dean's title in a book maybe

definitions.meaning: a dean presides over the body of clergy that runs a cathedral
the heading printed at the top of each section of a novel

explanation.definitionFit: Both the cleric presiding over a cathedral's governing clergy and a section heading.
